description: Per-skill evaluation for native-interop-engineer — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against library-linkage-architect / plugin-ecosystem-architect / api-designer, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when native code is called from a managed runtime
scenarios.input: We need to call a Rust image library from our Python service. How should we structure the boundary?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a memory-ownership question at a boundary
scenarios.input: Our JNI wrapper returns a pointer that the Java side frees. Is that correct?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for an intermittent boundary crash
scenarios.input: Our native extension crashes under load but never in our unit tests. Where do we look?

scenarios.description: The linkage form and ABI versioning belong to library-linkage-architect
scenarios.input: Should we statically or dynamically link our crypto library, and what soname policy should we use?

scenarios.description: Designing the extension platform belongs to plugin-ecosystem-architect
scenarios.input: Design the plugin marketplace and capability model for third-party extensions to our app.

scenarios.description: A network API contract belongs to api-designer
scenarios.input: Design our REST API for the inference service and its versioning strategy.

scenarios.description: Agent must require a named allocator and owner (R1)
scenarios.input: We'll just pass the pointer back to Python and let Python's GC free it. That should be fine.

scenarios.description: Agent must require a measured per-crossing cost (R2)
scenarios.input: We're moving our hot loop to C++ for speed. The FFI overhead shouldn't matter.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse exceptions crossing a foreign frame (R3)
scenarios.input: If the Rust code panics, the exception just propagates up through the JNI layer. It's handled at the top.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a colliding sentinel error value (R3)
scenarios.input: We return -1 to mean an error. The valid range is 0 to 1000 so -1 is safe.

scenarios.description: Agent must catch the guard re-entrancy deadlock (R4)
scenarios.input: Our native library calls a callback back into Python while it's iterating our list. Sometimes it hangs.

scenarios.description: Agent must not treat a binding library as the whole contract (R5)
scenarios.input: We're using a PyO3 binding library, so the memory management is handled for us.

patterns: handled for us, nothing to do

scenarios.description: Agent must demand justification before adding a boundary (R6)
scenarios.input: Let's add a Rust FFI layer for this feature. Rust is faster than our Go service.

patterns: Rust is faster so let's do it

scenarios.description: A full boundary design should surface ownership, errors, threads and cost
scenarios.input: Design the complete FFI boundary between our C++ engine and our .NET service.

scenarios.description: Agent should identify the callback-lifetime use-after-free
scenarios.input: Our callback sometimes fires after we've already shut down the object it references. We just log a warning.

scenarios.description: Output should be specific and actionable rather than hedged
scenarios.input: What is the most important thing to know about writing a native language binding?
